Weather Note: 🚨 CRITICAL WEATHER RISK: Cool temperatures (15–22°C) combined with high relative humidity (>90%) and rain/fog create EXTREME risk for rapid Phytophthora sporangia germination and epidemic canopy destruction.

🚨 COMBINED URGENCY WARNING: High visual disease coverage (45.0%) combined with elevated weather risk accelerates field epidemic spread! Immediate intervention required.

--- RECOMMENDED INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) PROTOCOL ---
1. CULTURAL CONTROL [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Destroy volunteer tomato/potato plants and infected crop residues. Space plants for maximum air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation.
2. BIOLOGICAL & BIO-RATIONAL CONTROL [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Apply copper octanoate or bio-control agents such as Bacillus subtilis preventively prior to wet cool weather events.
3. CHEMICAL CONTROL (Active Ingredients Only) [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Apply systemic oomyceticides (Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb, Dimethomorph, or Cymoxanil). Note: Active ingredients only. Registration status: UNVERIFIED -- requires current local label check.
   ⚠️ Note: Active ingredients only. Specific product dosage/PHI requires current local label/authority verification.

PREVENTION [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Plant resistant cultivars, monitor weather forecasts for late blight warnings, and maintain strict field hygiene.
SAFETY [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Wear chemical-resistant suit, neoprene gloves, and full face-shield when handling systemic oomyceticides.

output.weather_risk_note: Alternating wet and dry warm conditions (22–28°C) accelerate Alternaria solani secondary spore release.

   Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium fertilization. Practice 3-year crop rotation. Irrigate in early morning to allow canopy drying.
2. BIOLOGICAL & BIO-RATIONAL CONTROL [CIP International Potato Center - Level A2]:

3. CHEMICAL CONTROL (Active Ingredients Only) [CIP International Potato Center - Level A2]:
   Apply Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole premix. Note: Active ingredients only. Registration status: UNVERIFIED -- requires current local label check.
   ⚠️ Note: Active ingredients only. Specific product dosage/PHI requires current local label/authority verification.

PREVENTION [CIP International Potato Center - Level A2]:
   Use high-quality certified seed tubers, maintain vine nutrition, destroy haulms prior to harvest, and avoid tuber mechanical damage.
SAFETY [CIP International Potato Center - Level A2]:
   Wear protective gloves, eye goggles, and coveralls when applying fungicides.

Crop: Pepper | Diagnosis: Pepper_Bacterial_Spot
Confidence: 99.40% | EDL Uncertainty: 0.0800 | Status: ACCEPTED
Severity: Low (Visual Disease Coverage: 8.0%)
Location: Mirpurkhas, Sindh, Pakistan | Season: Summer
Weather Note: Warm rainy weather (24–30°C) with wind-driven rain splash accelerates Xanthomonas bacterial entry through stomata and wounds.

--- RECOMMENDED INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) PROTOCOL ---
1. CULTURAL CONTROL [Cornell University Extension Vegetable MD Online - Level B1]:
   Use certified disease-free seed. Practice 2–3 year crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation and work in fields only when foliage is dry.
2. BIOLOGICAL & BIO-RATIONAL CONTROL [Cornell University Extension Vegetable MD Online - Level B1]:
   Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis or bacteriophage products specific to Xanthomonas euvesicatoria.
3. CHEMICAL CONTROL (Active Ingredients Only) [Cornell University Extension Vegetable MD Online - Level B1]:
   Apply Copper Hydroxide combined with Mancozeb at early disease onset. Note: Active ingredients only. Registration status: UNVERIFIED -- requires current local label check.
   ⚠️ Note: Active ingredients only. Specific product dosage/PHI requires current local label/authority verification.

PREVENTION [Cornell University Extension Vegetable MD Online - Level B1]:
   Hot water seed treatment (50°C for 25 min), crop rotation, weed management, and drip irrigation.
SAFETY [Cornell University Extension Vegetable MD Online - Level B1]:
   Wear chemical gloves, protective suit, and eye protection during copper spraying.

test_case.title: Case 4: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (High Severity & Vector Weather)

output.weather_risk_note: ⚠️ VECTOR WEATHER RISK: Hot dry weather (>30°C) accelerates silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) vector reproduction and viral transmission rate.
output.advisory_english:
=== ZARI.ai DIAGNOSTIC & ADVISORY REPORT ===
Crop: Tomato | Diagnosis: Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus
Confidence: 99.10% | EDL Uncertainty: 0.0950 | Status: ACCEPTED
Severity: High (Visual Disease Coverage: 38.0%)
Location: Faisalabad, Punjab, Pakistan | Season: Summer
Weather Note: ⚠️ VECTOR WEATHER RISK: Hot dry weather (>30°C) accelerates silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) vector reproduction and viral transmission rate.

--- RECOMMENDED INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) PROTOCOL ---
1. CULTURAL CONTROL [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Install yellow sticky traps for whitefly monitoring. Cover seedbeds with 50-mesh insect-proof netting. Rogue out infected plants within 3 weeks of transplanting.
2. BIOLOGICAL & BIO-RATIONAL CONTROL [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Release whitefly natural enemies (Encarsia formosa or Eretmocerus eremicus). Apply Neem oil or Beauveria bassiana.
3. CHEMICAL CONTROL (Active Ingredients Only) [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Control whitefly vector using systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Acetamiprid, or Spirotetramat). Note: Direct virucides do not exist. Registration status: UNVERIFIED -- requires current local label check.
   ⚠️ Note: Active ingredients only. Specific product dosage/PHI requires current local label/authority verification.

PREVENTION [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrid varieties (Ty-1/Ty-3 genes), use 50-mesh netting, and clear weed hosts (Abutilon, Solanum nigrum).
SAFETY [CABI PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank - Level A2]:
   Wear chemical-resistant gloves, protective clothing, and respirator during vector spray operations.
